- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply after sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- In 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment volatility; smooth forecast curve with weighted average of recent 7-day sentiment-adjusted values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next 5 days.
